title: Post-reset: use case for quicker, more aggressive SL lock-in on fast moves (big impulse that is likely to bounce back fast): trigger, pricing, apply speed
roadmap_unmapped_reason: operator ask 2026-11-10; live-review / active-management design question for planning
note: Operator 2026-11-10 ~15:25Z (voice, condensed faithfully): 'There's a big jump, and it seems like we should be moving SLs ... put a note for after the reset to look at this as a use case of when we might need quicker and more aggressive action on an SL moving, because these seem like good points to be locking in, considering how quickly things are moving and the fact that they'll probably end up bouncing back fast.' CASE EVIDENCE (GET /api/bot/positions 15:21Z): ADA bybit_2 openR 0.90 = peakR (it was +0.08 at 15:04Z, so about +0.8R in ~17 min); XRP half bybit_2 openR 2.47 = peakR; SOL prop also moving. The operator-requested review lane session_01AFoLuKEWUfQBAMyZ68WS82 was dispatched at 15:44Z; append its outcome here. QUESTIONS FOR PLANNING: (1) a 'fast-move' wake: an R-velocity or ATR-impulse trigger (e.g. +X R in N minutes, or a bar range above k x ATR) that wakes LTR immediately instead of waiting for the 4h cadence or the 0.5R new_peak step; (2) price a 'lock-in on impulse' option in live_review_outcomes, conditioned on move speed and the mean-reversion probability after impulses, net of cost and pre-registered (the current table conditions on peak/open/bars, not velocity, so it may not see a fast bounce); (3) apply latency: tightens are advice-only today, so an operator-approved lock-in needs a sub-minute directed path (TRADE-ACTION-FAST-PATH) or, if the evidence supports it, a proposed mandate for impulse lock-ins; (4) the 13:33Z ADA case: a +0.64R intrabar extreme was given back to +0.08R within ~90 min (PEAK-FLOOR-OPEN-R); count how often that happens across legs; (5) related rows: PEAK-FLOOR-OPEN-R, TRADE-ACTION-FAST-PATH, LTR-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ACTIONS, the Active-management doctrine (ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL 'Active management': every action class advice-only until its own net-of-cost test passes). Output: a pre-registered queue unit plus build rows; no live change from this row. 2026-11-10 ~15:50Z: during the move the operator hand-moved the breakout_2 SOL stop 85.5 -> 82.5 (locks about +3.51R / $35.05 gross on entry 87.64, qty 6.82). Operator ADDITION, verbatim gist: also look after the reset at whether this is a use case where MOVING THE TAKE-PROFIT would help as well as moving SLs (e.g. extend the TP on a fast impulse while locking the stop, or pull it in to bank before the expected bounce). Price both directions under the TP doctrine (ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL 'TP doctrine' and 'Active management': a TP move is an action class, advice-only until its own net-of-cost test passes). 2026-11-10 ~15:50Z operator ONE-TIME pre-approval, verbatim: 'In this situation, because we want to move fast, I want to pre-approve accepting the advice of the LTR session, so that we can make that immediate and not have to wait for my response after it finishes.' Scope: the 15:44Z review lane (ADA/XRP/SOL prop) only; tighten only; breakout_2 left to the operator; applied via the operator-directed path. NOT a standing mandate. Planning question it raises: should a 'fast-move pre-approval' exist as a PROPOSED mandate (operator grants), so the next impulse doesn't need a chat round-trip? The operator explicitly wants speed here. 2026-11-10 15:51-15:52Z outcome of the operator-pre-approved fast-move review (lane session_01AFoLuKEWUfQBAMyZ68WS82; advice at 15:50Z: XRP tighten 1.0557, SOL prop 83.22 on tradeify_1/velotrade_1, ADA hold). The lane declined to apply: it treated the relayed pre-approval as information, and it had no diag token for read-back. The MANAGER applied via scripts/ops/directed_action.py (operator quote recorded). XRP pkg-633f05fad1ee4c1d: APPLIED and read back, venue SL 1.0629 on bybit_2 + bybit_portfolio (clipped from 1.0557 to the 1xATR noise floor), TP 1.0271; push->done 11.4s. SOL prop pkg-50f5eed272f64197 tradeify_1 + velotrade_1: NOT APPLIED, 'package not open': directed_actions has no prop apply path (prop tickets live in the prop journal, not order_packages; the LTR-8 gap), so the operator must move prop stops by hand. Lessons for planning: (1) a relayed operator approval is not accepted by lanes, so fast-move applies must go through the manager or a granted mandate; (2) lanes need diag read access for read-back; (3) prop needs an apply path (phone_trail.request_sl_tighten from directed actions), which PHONE-LIVE-ACCOUNT-FEED also needs. 2026-11-10 16:13Z CASE DATA POINT: ADA bybit_2 (pkg-3de13868d406447a) peaked at +1.37R and gave back 0.52R within minutes (giveback wake at 16:11:36Z). That is the fast bounce the operator predicted at 15:25Z. The 15:50Z review held ADA: the tightest allowed stop was 0.17549 (+0.49R), and the 15:06Z priced cell was hold +1.334R vs breakeven +0.98. Use as a labelled example when testing a fast-move lock-in rule; the outcome will be known when the trade closes. 2026-11-10 OUTCOME: XRP half (pkg-633f05fad1ee4c1d, bybit_2) STOPPED OUT at 18:29:19Z on the locked stop 1.0629 (applied 15:51Z under the operator's pre-approval): reason sl, PnL +$2.4542 (+4.1%) on bybit_2 real money. The mirror bybit_portfolio closed too (PnL not priced). The lock kept about +1.74R of a +2.89R peak; without it the original SL 1.1411 would still be open. A clean labelled example for the fast-move lock-in study. Note: the 20:09Z review was briefed that the short was still open (manager brief stale); the venue/journal read at 20:15Z shows only the new ml_entry LONG (93 @ 1.0654, opened 20:02:30Z), so there was no netting conflict.
